passages.title: 우리 강아지 콩이
passages.passage: I have a small dog. His name is Kong. He is brown and white. Kong is three years old. Every morning, I walk with him in the park. He likes to run after the ball. After the walk, he drinks a lot of water and sleeps on my bed. Kong is my best friend.

qs.e: He is brown and white 라고 나와요.
Every morning, I walk with him in the park.
sleeps on my bed.

passages.title: 내 생일 파티
passages.passage: Last Saturday was my birthday. My mom made a big chocolate cake. Five friends came to my house. We played games and sang songs. My best friend gave me a book about animals. I was very happy. It was the best day of the year.

qs.e: Last Saturday was my birthday.
gave me a book about animals.
Five friends came to my house.

passages.title: 학교 도서관 안내
passages.passage: The school library is open from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays. Students may borrow up to three books at a time for two weeks. If you return a book late, you cannot borrow books for one week. Eating and drinking are not allowed inside. On Fridays, the library closes early at 3 p.m. for cleaning.

qs.p: 한 번에 몇 권까지 빌릴 수 있나요?
qs.e: borrow up to three books at a time.
you cannot borrow books for one week.
On Fridays, the library closes early at 3 p.m.

passages.title: 펭귄의 겨울나기
passages.passage: Emperor penguins live in Antarctica, the coldest place on Earth. In winter, the temperature falls below minus 50 degrees. To stay warm, hundreds of penguins stand close together in a big group. The birds on the outside slowly move to the middle, and the ones in the middle move out. In this way, every penguin gets a turn in the warm center.

qs.e: hundreds of penguins stand close together.
outside → middle, middle → out 으로 교대해요.
추위 대응 방식이 글 전체의 중심 내용이에요.

passages.title: 재활용 캠페인
passages.passage: Our town started a new recycling program last month. Residents now separate paper, plastic, glass, and food waste into four different bins. At first, many people found the new rules confusing, so the town hall printed simple guides and put them in every mailbox. After only four weeks, the amount of trash sent to the landfill dropped by almost thirty percent. The mayor says the goal is fifty percent by next year.

qs.e: paper, plastic, glass, and food waste = 4가지.
many people found the new rules confusing.
dropped by almost thirty percent.

passages.title: 잠을 자는 이유
passages.passage: Scientists once believed that sleep was simply a time when the body rested. Recent studies, however, show that the brain is very busy during sleep. It sorts through the day's events, keeps what matters, and throws away what does not. Teenagers need about nine hours of sleep, but most get fewer than seven. Students who sleep well remember lessons better and feel less stressed during exams.

qs.e: sorts through the day's events, keeps what matters.
Teenagers need about nine hours.
remember lessons better and feel less stressed.

passages.title: 자원봉사 모집
passages.passage: The Riverside Animal Shelter is looking for weekend volunteers. No experience is necessary; training is provided on your first day. Volunteers help feed the animals, clean the cages, and walk the dogs. You must be at least fourteen years old, and anyone under eighteen needs a parent's signature. Volunteers who complete twenty hours receive a certificate that can be used for school records.

qs.e: at least fourteen years old, 경험은 불필요.
anyone under eighteen needs a parent's signature.
receive a certificate for school records.

passages.title: 커피의 여행
passages.passage: Coffee did not always come in paper cups. The plant was first discovered in Ethiopia, where a goatherd noticed his animals became lively after eating certain red berries. From there, coffee traveled to Arabia, where the first coffee houses opened in the fifteenth century. These shops became centers of conversation and news, so much so that some rulers tried to close them, fearing that people were talking too freely.

qs.e: first discovered in Ethiopia.
became lively after eating certain red berries.

qs.p: 일부 통치자들이 커피하우스를 닫으려 한 이유는?
qs.e: fearing that people were talking too freely.

passages.title: 도시의 자전거 공유
passages.passage: Bike-sharing systems have spread to more than a thousand cities worldwide. The idea is simple: users unlock a bike with a phone app, ride it, and leave it at any station. Supporters point out that the systems reduce traffic and pollution while improving public health. Critics, however, note that abandoned bikes can block sidewalks, and that in some cities thousands of unused bikes have piled up in vacant lots. The most successful programs are those where the city sets clear limits on how many bikes each company may release.

qs.e: reduce traffic and pollution while improving public health.
abandoned bikes can block sidewalks.
the city sets clear limits on how many bikes.

passages.title: 소음과 집중력
passages.passage: Many students claim they study better with music, but the research is more complicated. Studies suggest that quiet instrumental music can help with repetitive tasks such as copying notes. For work that requires reading and understanding, however, songs with words interfere, because the brain processes the lyrics as language and competes with the text on the page. The safest rule is this: the harder the material, the quieter the room should be.

qs.e: quiet instrumental music can help with repetitive tasks.

qs.p: 가사 있는 노래가 방해가 되는 이유는?
c: 뇌가 가사를 언어로 처리해 글과 경쟁해서
qs.e: the brain processes the lyrics as language.
the harder the material, the quieter the room.

passages.title: 기억의 궁전
passages.passage: Long before printing, orators memorized speeches lasting hours by using a technique called the memory palace. The speaker imagines a familiar building and places each idea in a specific room. To recall the speech, he simply walks through the building in his mind. The method works because human memory is far better at storing places and images than abstract words. Modern memory champions still rely on it, and studies of their brains show no unusual structure, only well-practiced habits.

c: 익숙한 건물의 각 방에 생각을 배치한다
qs.e: places each idea in a specific room.
memory is far better at storing places and images.
no unusual structure, only well-practiced habits.

passages.title: 사라지는 모래
passages.passage: Sand may seem endless, but usable sand is running short. Desert sand, shaped by wind, is too round to bind in concrete, so builders depend on river and coastal sand. As construction booms, illegal mining has stripped riverbeds in several countries, causing bridges to collapse and salt water to seep into farmland. Researchers are testing concrete made with crushed glass and recycled rubble, but scaling such alternatives to the size of the global construction industry remains a distant goal.

qs.p: 사막 모래를 콘크리트에 쓸 수 없는 이유는?
c: 바람에 깎여 너무 둥글어서 잘 붙지 않는다
qs.e: too round to bind in concrete.

qs.p: 불법 채취가 초래한 피해가 아닌 것은?
qs.e: 사막 확대는 언급되지 않았어요.

c: 유리·잔해 활용을 시험 중이나 규모 확대는 멀다
qs.e: scaling such alternatives ... remains a distant goal.

passages.title: 군중의 지혜
passages.passage: In 1906, the statistician Francis Galton attended a country fair where villagers guessed the weight of an ox. No single guess was correct, yet the average of nearly eight hundred guesses fell within one pound of the true weight. Galton, who had expected to demonstrate the foolishness of crowds, instead documented what is now called the wisdom of crowds. The effect holds only under specific conditions: the guessers must be numerous, independent, and diverse. When people can hear one another, the errors stop canceling out and the group drifts toward whatever the loudest voice suggests.

c: 약 800명 추측의 평균이 실제와 거의 일치했다
qs.e: the average ... fell within one pound of the true weight.
had expected to demonstrate the foolishness of crowds.
When people can hear one another, the errors stop canceling out.

passages.title: 빛 공해
passages.passage: Artificial light has extended the working day, but it has also erased the night sky for most of humanity. More than eighty percent of the world's population now lives under skies bright enough to hide the Milky Way. The consequences reach beyond astronomy. Migrating birds, which navigate by stars, collide with illuminated towers; sea turtle hatchlings crawl toward streetlights instead of the ocean. Encouragingly, the remedy is unusually simple and cheap: shielded fixtures that point downward, and warmer bulbs that scatter less. Several cities that adopted such rules reported measurable improvements within a single year.

qs.p: 인공 빛의 영향으로 언급되지 않은 것은?
qs.e: 농작물은 언급되지 않았어요.

c: 아래를 향한 차폐 조명과 따뜻한 색 전구
qs.e: shielded fixtures that point downward, and warmer bulbs.
reported measurable improvements within a single year.

passages.title: 재택근무 보고서
passages.passage: A two-year study of 1,600 employees at a technology firm produced mixed findings on remote work. Productivity on individual tasks rose by roughly thirteen percent, largely because workers took shorter breaks and lost no commuting time. Collaboration, however, suffered: the number of messages exchanged between different departments fell by a quarter, and new employees reported feeling isolated. The company ultimately adopted a hybrid schedule, requiring three office days per week, with Tuesdays reserved for cross-team meetings.

qs.e: rose by roughly thirteen percent.

c: 부서 간 소통 감소와 신입의 고립감
qs.e: messages between departments fell by a quarter.
hybrid schedule, requiring three office days per week.

passages.title: 고객 만족도 조사 결과
passages.passage: Our annual survey collected responses from 4,200 customers. Overall satisfaction reached 87 percent, up four points from last year. Respondents praised the speed of delivery, with 92 percent reporting that orders arrived on or before the promised date. The lowest-rated area was the return process, which only 61 percent described as easy. Written comments frequently mentioned the difficulty of printing return labels at home. In response, the company will introduce label-free returns at partner drop-off points beginning in the third quarter.

qs.e: The lowest-rated area was the return process (61%).
difficulty of printing return labels at home.
label-free returns at partner drop-off points.

passages.title: 관찰자 효과
passages.passage: In the 1920s, researchers at a factory tested whether brighter lighting would raise output. It did. Then they dimmed the lights, and output rose again. The unsettling conclusion was that the workers were responding not to illumination but to being studied. Later reanalysis has questioned the original data, and the size of the effect is now considered far smaller than once claimed. Yet the underlying caution endures: in any study of human behavior, the act of measurement may alter the very thing being measured, which is why well-designed trials conceal from participants which group they belong to.

c: 조명을 밝게 해도 어둡게 해도 생산성이 올랐다
qs.e: 밝게 → 상승, 어둡게 → 또 상승.

c: 효과 크기가 예전 주장보다 훨씬 작다
qs.e: the size of the effect is now considered far smaller.

qs.p: 잘 설계된 실험이 참가자에게 감추는 것은?
qs.e: conceal from participants which group they belong to.

passages.title: 번역할 수 없는 말
passages.passage: Every language contains words that resist translation, not because equivalents are missing but because the surrounding assumptions differ. The Japanese term for the light filtering through leaves compresses an entire aesthetic tradition into three syllables; rendering it in English requires a clause. Some scholars once argued that such gaps constrain thought itself, a strong claim that experiments have largely deflated. What survives is a weaker but more interesting version: language does not build walls around thinking, but it does lay paths, making some ideas quicker to reach than others.

qs.p: 번역이 어려운 진짜 이유로 글이 제시한 것은?
qs.e: not because equivalents are missing but because the surrounding assumptions differ.
a strong claim that experiments have largely deflated.

c: 언어는 사고에 길을 놓아 어떤 생각을 더 쉽게 만든다
qs.e: it does lay paths, making some ideas quicker to reach.

passages.title: 박물관 관람 안내
passages.passage: Welcome to the City History Museum. Photography without flash is permitted in all galleries except the textile room, where light damages the fabric. Guided tours in English begin at 10:30 and 14:00 from the main desk and last about fifty minutes. Backpacks larger than a laptop bag must be left in the free lockers near the entrance. The rooftop café closes thirty minutes before the museum, so plan your visit accordingly.

qs.e: except the textile room, where light damages the fabric.
last about fifty minutes.
must be left in the free lockers near the entrance.

passages.title: 우리 학교 텃밭
passages.passage: Last spring, our class started a small garden behind the school. We planted tomatoes, lettuce, and strawberries. At first, the plants grew slowly because we watered them too much. Our science teacher explained that roots also need air, and that soaked soil pushes the air out. After we watered less often, the plants became healthy. In June, we harvested enough vegetables to make salads for the whole grade.

qs.p: 처음에 식물이 잘 자라지 않은 이유는?
qs.e: the plants grew slowly because we watered them too much.
roots also need air, and soaked soil pushes the air out.

c: 학년 전체가 먹을 샐러드를 만들 만큼 수확했다
qs.e: harvested enough vegetables to make salads for the whole grade.

passages.title: 물의 순환
passages.passage: Water on Earth never disappears; it only changes form. Heat from the sun turns water in oceans and lakes into vapor, which rises into the air. High above the ground, the vapor cools and becomes tiny drops that form clouds. When the drops grow heavy enough, they fall as rain or snow. Some of this water flows back to the sea, and the cycle begins again. The water you drink today may have fallen as rain a thousand years ago.

qs.e: Heat from the sun turns water ... into vapor.

c: 수증기가 식어 작은 물방울이 되어 모인다
qs.e: the vapor cools and becomes tiny drops that form clouds.

c: 비는 천 년에 한 번 온다
qs.e: 물이 순환한다는 주제를 인상적으로 마무리한 문장이에요.

passages.title: 새 이웃
passages.passage: A new family moved into the house next door on Monday. They have a daughter named Sujin. She is in my grade but goes to a different school. On Tuesday, my mother made kimchi stew and asked me to bring some to them. Sujin opened the door and smiled. We talked about music for almost an hour. Now we walk to the bus stop together every morning.

qs.e: in my grade but goes to a different school.
asked me to bring some to them.

qs.p: 지금 두 사람은 아침마다 무엇을 하나요?
qs.e: we walk to the bus stop together every morning.

passages.title: 가짜 뉴스 판별법
passages.passage: Professional fact-checkers do not read suspicious articles the way most people do. Rather than studying the page carefully from top to bottom, they leave it almost immediately, opening new tabs to see what other sources say about the site itself. Researchers call this lateral reading. Students trained in the method identified misleading pages far more often than those who relied on surface signals such as a professional design or a long list of references, both of which are easy to fake.

c: 즉시 다른 탭을 열어 그 사이트의 평판을 확인한다
qs.e: opening new tabs to see what other sources say — lateral reading.
Researchers call this lateral reading.

qs.p: 쉽게 위조할 수 있다고 언급된 것은?
qs.e: both of which are easy to fake.

passages.title: 달력의 열한 날
passages.passage: In September 1752, Britain went to sleep on the second and woke on the fourteenth. The country was abandoning the Julian calendar, which had drifted eleven days out of step with the sun over the centuries. Popular histories claim that mobs rioted, demanding their lost days back, but historians find little evidence for such protests. What did cause genuine confusion was money: rents and wages had to be recalculated, and workers reasonably asked whether they should be paid for days that no longer existed.

qs.e: slept on the 2nd, woke on the 14th — 11일이 건너뛰어졌어요.

qs.p: 폭동에 관한 이야기에 대해 역사학자들의 견해는?
qs.e: historians find little evidence for such protests.
rents and wages had to be recalculated.
